The Pee Dee River empties into Winyah Bay, which opens into the **Atlantic Ocean**.  
The first serious effort to cut a sea‑link between that Atlantic coast and the Pacific, cutting through the continental region that contains the **El Valle** volcano in Panama, was the **French Panama Canal project**.  

That project was headed by **Ferdinand de Lesseps**, the French civil engineer who had built the Suez Canal. He led the French attempt to construct a canal through Panama in the 1880s (the effort ultimately failed and was later succeeded by the U.S. project).
